title: CIP: Update vendor list
description:
Updated vendors from a vid file that was kindly provided to me from ODVA I wrote a small python script to read the ODVA file and output in a predefined format, so i can update vendors in different tools.
To preserve obsolete vendors, i issue a list of them separately. Some company names have special UTF-8 characters like `ü`, `ä`, `ç`, `ã` and `）/ U+FF09` and I'm not sure if Wireshark can handle them at this place in code.
Can someone please acknowledge that this is ok? There were some `Reserved` entries in the list and also some gaps. So i presume that it doesn't matter if one value is missing.
Currently i did set up my script to fill all gaps with `Reserved` entries to better match the current version (diffs are smaller).
Should i remove all `Reserved` entries, to have a more clean list instead? Patch from https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/b31a6aaae75623df7790fcd7c051d402b7a9263e was not applied, as they are still listed with the "old" company name @[ODVA](https://marketplace.odva.org/organizations/129-bernecker-rainer-industrie-elektronik-gmbh) and therefore is the right value for me.
Is the original issue accessible somewhere, so we can contact the corresponding person or should i just manually patch it to the `B&R` value? Hoping i didn't missed anything regarding creating a merge request (new to Wireshark development).

@rknall for B&R part ?

Personally, I don't care anymore as I am not working there. But it hardly surprises me, that they never bothered to register the name-change with the ODVA. @PhilippHaefele the company changed the name in 2017 to "B&R Industrial Automation GmbH" as it was never known for Bernecker+Rainer outside of Austria and as soon as ABB bought them, they thought about getting it right. 

Well, as I said, personally I don't mind changing it back, but the users will not be able to make the correlation in most places and might mistake equipment.

As a side-note, B&R might not be the only company which did not change their official registration name and therefore the ODVA lists may be massively out of date. Not a stopping block per-se, just something to keep in mind.

I just checked some EDS files and most of them use old company names with `Bernecker + Rainer` init.

There's only one EDS file with `ModifiedBy=B&R Industrial Automation GmbH` in the `FileInfo` and VendorName being `Schneider Electric (resold by B&R Industrial Automation GmbH)`.

All other products seem to be release before they were sold in 2017, so maybe that's why they didn't changed it yet.

So PLC/equipment users will most likely be used to the old company name in their PLC configuration tools.

Haven't got a personal preference either here, i normally just tending to be as near to the protocol / ODVA definitions as possible as they define the system.

@rknall & @alagoutte How do we proceed here?

I`m fine to keep the values like they are coming from ODVA for me and in my opinion i would forward the companies to ODVA if they complain that something is wrong as this is the right place to fix it.
Ok for keep value for ODVA for me

> Some company names have special UTF-8 characters like `ü`, `ä`, `ç`, `ã` and `）/ U+FF09` and I'm not sure if Wireshark can handle them at this place in code.  
> Can someone please acknowledge that this is ok?

That's OK. `doc/README.developer` says

> Source files can use UTF-8 encoding, but characters outside the ASCII
> range should be used sparingly. It should be safe to use non-ASCII
> characters in comments and strings, but some compilers (such as GCC
> versions prior to 10) may not support extended identifiers very well.
> There is also no guarantee that a developer's text editor will interpret
> the characters the way you intend them to be interpreted.

and your usage appears to fall well within that description.
Thanks, so i will leave them as they are. Didn't got that sentence in den developer README somehow.

Has someone an opinion regarding the `Reserved` entries?

Can someone tell, what value is shown when vendor ID is not in the list (can't simulate that right now as i do not have any suitable equipment at my place, to check a connection with a unknown vendorID)?

What's there to opine about the "Reserved" entries? If the ODVA list says "Reserved", then that's the proper string to use.

Regarding the vendor ID that's not in the list; looking at the code I think it won't show any string at all, since there was no match.

Thanks for your reply (especially regarding the implementation details)

The interesting thing is that some "Reserved" values, got actual values (e.g. the very low value 79 or 157).

So from my side i do not see any reasonable value for having "Reserved" at all, but added them in the first place for a much smaller diff.

As i got more details regarding the implementation i will recreate the list with the "Reserved" value like they are in ODVA list and leave off all values that are not in ODVA list or my `obsolete_vids` list.

format, so i can update vendors in different tools.
